subject: program distance data setup for importing,

messages.author: 67ffbd21ef458ea8
messages.subject: program distance data setup for importing,
parts:
I'd appreciate any help anyone can provide. I'm pretty new to distance
sampling, and would like to use the program DISTANCE to calculate
population estimates of mottled ducks. The survey has 8 transects and 2
point counts. I have the lengths and areas of each. The survey is
conducted every 2 weeks all year long. For the past 2 years, we've been
collecting distance data on mottled ducks.

My question is hopefully simple- what's the best way to set up the data
for importing and analysis?

I've looked through the documentation, and couldn't really find how to
deal with time series. Should I count every biweekly survey as a separate
estimate?

Peter Keller

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: program distance data setup for importing,
parts:
Peter-

I know zilch about mottled ducks, your eventual goals for the work and
how many detections you will get per survey and inter-transect
variability. Each is essential
to answer your questions. Also, you said you have 8 transects and 2
point counts. Do you really mean that you have a
combined line transect and point transect survey? If so, there is no
way to handle that in Distance. Never run into a situation in which
both types were needed for a single analysis. That will be a problem.
With regard to your question about time series. There is no
specific way to handle time series in Distance. If you want an estimate
for each 2-week period, set up the survey periods as strata and select
the option to
compute a separate estimate for each stratum. You can still pool across
strata to estimate detection probability if needed or you can use covariates
that may change detection probability within and across strata.

regards--jeff
